page: Microsoft Azure E48d_v4 is an EDv4-family virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, the server features 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes a dedicated CPU allocation, 35 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is bundled with 1843 GB of local storage and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory operations. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 11270.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 38601.34. Memory bandwidth is measured at 165.21 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 83.52 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database operations on Passmark scored 16136.08, while Redis SET operations reached 40.15 million operations per second.

Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded compression and large-scale language model execution. Single-threaded gzip compression performed in the bottom 25% at 23.78 GB/sec, and LLM text generation speeds for a medium 7B model were limited to 7.03 tokens per second. However, the high memory density and bundled 1843 GB local storage make this server well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, relational databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications that require a balance of high RAM capacity and local disk space.
